criteria_applied_identically: Direct relevance to locked L3 coverage or a necessary counter-evidence/protocol guardrail
Canonical identity and metadata verifiable from a source of record
Non-duplicative claim-level value after family/version grouping
Authority and inspectable original-content path for production-intended use
No inference from paper-native metrics to the v5 benchmark and no inference that literature proves H3

dispositions.old_identity: Rakesh Agrawal and Ramakrishnan Srikant (1994), Fast Algorithms for Mining Association Rules in Large Databases
dispositions.reason: Foundational source-of-record for support, confidence, frequent itemsets, and Apriori-family mining; retained only for mining semantics, not ranking effectiveness.
verification_basis: Canonical title, two full authors, year, venue, pages, and no assigned DOI verified

dispositions.old_identity: Abhijeet Ghoshal and Sumit Sarkar (2014), Association Rules for Recommendations with Multiple Items
dispositions.reason: Direct association-rule recommendation study with multi-item consequents and comparator evidence; provides non-redundant claim-level value.

dispositions.old_identity: Duen-Ren Liu, Chin-Hui Lai, and Wang-Jung Lee (2009), A Hybrid of Sequential Rules and Collaborative Filtering for Product Recommendation
dispositions.reason: Audit-core historical hybrid precedent. Retained with metadata-only/content-unverified restrictions; the exact 2009 full work remains queued.
verification_basis: 2007 conference predecessor tracked separately in the same family

dispositions.old_identity: Heng-Tze Cheng and 15 named coauthors (2016), Wide & Deep Learning for Recommender Systems
dispositions.reason: Foundational joint-training and component-comparison precedent; full 16-author metadata and original content are now verified.

dispositions.old_identity: Wang-Cheng Kang and Julian McAuley (2018), Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
dispositions.reason: Canonical causal self-attentive sequential baseline and objective reference; retained with next-item and sampled-evaluation limitations.

dispositions.old_identity: Fei Sun, Jun Liu, Jian Wu, Changhua Pei, Xiao Lin, Wenwu Ou, and Peng Jiang (2019), BERT4Rec
dispositions.reason: Canonical masked bidirectional sequential objective reference; retained with next-item and sampled-evaluation limitations.

dispositions.old_identity: Bo Peng, Zhiyun Ren, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, and Xia Ning (2022), HAM: Hybrid Associations Models for Sequential Recommendation
dispositions.reason: Non-redundant learned-association hybrid and component-ablation precedent; explicitly separated from Apriori mining.

dispositions.old_identity: Bo Peng, Zhiyun Ren, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, and Xia Ning (2023), M²: Mixed Models with Preferences, Popularities and Transitions for Next-Basket Recommendation
dispositions.reason: Direct mixed-component next-basket model and ablation precedent; adds basket-native coverage not supplied by sequential next-item papers.

dispositions.old_identity: Ming Li, Sami Jullien, Mozhdeh Ariannezhad, and Maarten de Rijke (2023), A Next Basket Recommendation Reality Check
dispositions.reason: Audit-core evidence for repeat/explore decomposition, frequency baselines, and evaluation confounding.

dispositions.old_identity: Ming Li, Mozhdeh Ariannezhad, Andrew Yates, and Maarten de Rijke (2023), Masked and Swapped Sequence Modeling for Next Novel Basket Recommendation in Grocery Shopping
dispositions.reason: Direct next-novel-basket paper and BTBR baseline with useful strategy-level counter-evidence.

dispositions.old_identity: Ming Li, Ali Vardasbi, Andrew Yates, and Maarten de Rijke (2023), Repetition and Exploration in Sequential Recommendation
dispositions.reason: Direct diagnostic evidence for repetition bias and exploration-only analysis; complements basket-specific evidence.

dispositions.old_identity: Danil Gusak, Anna Volodkevich, Anton Klenitskiy, Alexey Vasilev, and Evgeny Frolov (2025), Time to Split: Exploring Data Splitting Strategies for Offline Evaluation of Sequential Recommenders
dispositions.reason: Audit-core protocol evidence that split choice changes evaluation outcomes and can change model rankings; old-lane identity was reverified from the full accepted author version.

dispositions.old_identity: Weiyang Lin, Sergio A. Alvarez, and Carolina Ruiz (2002), Efficient Adaptive-Support Association Rule Mining for Recommender Systems
dispositions.reason: Relevant but redundant legacy rule-recommender method; Ghoshal and Sarkar provides stronger direct multi-item recommendation coverage, while Apriori supplies the foundational definitions. Retention would inflate the corpus without a necessary claim card.
verification_basis: Official DOI 10.1023/A:1013284820704 and bibliographic record verified

dispositions.old_identity: Zhiang Wu, Changsheng Li, Jie Cao, and Yong Ge (2020), On Scalability of Association-rule-based Recommendation: A Unified Distributed-computing Framework
dispositions.reason: Scaling/serving focus does not add claim-level value for the locked mechanism, objective, repeat/explore, or attribution questions.

dispositions.old_identity: Mozhdeh Ariannezhad, Sami Jullien, Ming Li, Min Fang, Sebastian Schelter, and Maarten de Rijke (2022), ReCANet
dispositions.reason: Repeat-consumption model is misaligned with the locked novel-purchase target and is redundant with retained counter-evidence on repeat dominance.

dispositions.old_identity: Ori Katz, Oren Barkan, Nir Zabari, and Noam Koenigstein (2022), Learning to Ride a Buy-Cycle: A Hyper-Convolutional Model for Next Basket Recommendation
dispositions.reason: Repurchase/buy-cycle target is not a suitable direct baseline for the locked organic-novel target; no unique claim card remains after repeat/explore sources are retained.

dispositions.reason: Replaced by the broader peer-reviewed systematic review and replicability study of BERT4Rec, which has stronger claim-level coverage of implementation and training-budget sensitivity and a lawful full artifact.
